executive_summary: GWP grew 7.6% to A$18,412m (FY25: A$17,106m) driven predominantly by the 10-month RACQI acquisition contribution of A$1,272m; underlying organic GWP growth was only 1.9%, exposing the acquisition-dependency of the headline growth narrative

The one thing investors should focus on: NPAT fell 24.8% to A$1,022m (FY25: A$1,359m) as FY25 was inflated by favourable perils and a BI reserve release — the reported insurance margin contracted 280bps to 14.7%; underlying insurance margin also slipped 50bps to 15.0%, but ex-RACQI improved 50bps to 16.0%, indicating RACQI dilution is the key margin headwind

Red flag: RACQI posted a A$174m insurance loss in 1H26 (before recovering to A$79m profit in 2H26), natural perils costs came in A$114m above allowance at A$1,579m, and the pending RAC Insurance (WA) acquisition will consume ~0.36x CET1, pushing pro-forma CET1 to ~1.00x — at the lower bound of the 0.9-1.1x target range with limited buffer

key_numbers.ebitda_margin: Reported insurance margin 14.7% vs 17.5% (-280bps); underlying insurance margin 15.0% vs 15.5% (-50bps); ex-RACQI underlying margin 16.0% vs 15.5% (+50bps)
key_numbers.npat_statutory: A$1,022m vs A$1,359m (-24.8%); FY25 elevated by favourable perils and BI reserve release
key_numbers.npat_underlying: Underlying insurance profit A$1,578m vs A$1,542m (+2.3%); difference to statutory NPAT reflects perils above allowance (-A$114m net), lower investment income on technical reserves (A$246m vs A$464m due to -A$136m risk-free rate impact), higher non-controlling interests (A$195m vs A$176m), and tax/interest; reconciliation to NPAT not fully bridged in the presentation
key_numbers.eps: Not disclosed in presentation; payout ratio of 74% on 32cps total dividend implies NPAT-per-share can be inferred but EPS figure not explicitly stated
key_numbers.net_debt_cash: Not disclosed explicitly; CET1 ratio 1.14x PCA at Jun-26 vs 1.18x at Dec-25; completed A$200m on-market buyback at avg ~A$7.30/share; interest expense A$190m (FY26) vs A$192m (FY25); gross debt level not disclosed in this presentation

analysis.quality_of_earnings: Investment income on technical reserves collapsed to A$246m from A$464m, driven by a A$136m adverse risk-free rate mark-to-market impact — this is an IFRS 17 accounting artefact that suppresses reported profit but reverses over time (exit yield ~5.5% suggests underlying income recovery). Reserve releases of A$78m in IIA supported reported profit and the underlying margin; without these, IIA underlying profit would have been flat-to-down. The presentation does not disclose operating cashflow or free cashflow, preventing assessment of cash conversion quality. RACQI contributed a net loss in 1H26 of A$174m before recovering, and management confirm all integration/amortisation costs are included in underlying — reducing the risk of hidden below-the-line charges but making the underlying margin look temporarily depressed.
analysis.management_framing: Mixed — leaning Promotional. The deck leads with '7.6% GWP growth' and 'Strong FY26 results' while burying the fact that organic underlying GWP growth was only 1.9% and NPAT fell 24.8%. The 24.8% NPAT decline is immediately contextualised as a FY25 base effect, which is partially fair but deflects from RACQI's 1H26 A$174m insurance loss. The ex-RACQI underlying margin of 16.0% is prominently featured to offset the total reported margin compression. Operating cashflow and free cashflow are not disclosed, which is a transparency gap for an insurer of this scale. The 'perils upside' slide promoting ~$100m average benefit from reinsurance cover is forward-looking marketing without historical calibration context.
positives: Underlying insurance profit rose 2.3% to A$1,578m despite RACQI drag, weaker NZD, and lower investment income — driven by 50bps improvement in underlying claims ratio to 51.6% and 120bps improvement in expense ratio to 22.6%; administration ratio ex-levies improved 60bps to 11.6% with guidance for sub-11% in FY27

NZ Retail delivered a standout underlying insurance margin of 25.3% (NZD basis), up from 23.0% in FY25, with NZD GWP growing 3.7% and direct customer volumes +80k; tNPS improved materially across all divisions (AU: 45.1 to 54.7, NZ: 54.5 to 63.0); RACQI synergies exceeded A$50m annually and the 2H26 RACQI insurance profit of A$79m signals integration traction

FY27 guidance of 14.5%-16.5% reported insurance margin with 5%-8% GWP growth is credible and conservative; perils reinsurance cover provides ~A$1bn of additional annual protection for 3 years with modelled average upside of ~A$100m (approximately 1% margin benefit) to the perils allowance; FY27 perils allowance rising only ~2% despite RACQI inclusion is capital-efficient
negatives: RACQI was materially dilutive in FY26: the division posted a A$174m insurance loss in 1H26 from severe perils before its portfolio was integrated into IAG's group reinsurance program, contributing to A$114m net perils overrun for the year; the underlying RIA margin including RACQI was 14.7% vs 16.4% ex-RACQI, flagging ongoing acquisition earnings drag

NZ Intermediated (NZI) is deteriorating: NZD GWP declined 11.0%, underlying insurance profit fell 18.9% to NZD$133m, and underlying margin compressed to 14.1% from 16.2%, with a soft commercial market and no clear recovery catalyst disclosed; NZ as a whole saw reported insurance profit fall A$139m in AUD terms

Balance sheet buffer is thin post-RAC Insurance WA acquisition: pro-forma CET1 of ~1.00x sits at the bottom of the 0.9-1.1x target range; management acknowledge 'comfort to operate at lower end' but this leaves limited room for a severe perils year or adverse reserve development, and the A$200m buyback completed at ~A$7.30 per share may prove capital-destructive if RAC Insurance integration pressures emerge

bottom_line.bull: IAG's underlying economics are improving — claims ratio trending down, expense ratio heading below 11%, RACQI integration synergies achieved and 2H26 returning to profit, reinsurance providing structural perils downside protection, and FY27 guidance implies a step-up in reported margin to 14.5-16.5% on growing GWP; if perils are benign and NZI stabilises, NPAT could recover to A$1.2-1.3bn+.
bottom_line.bear: Organic GWP growth of only 1.9% strips away the acquisition-driven headline; RACQI integration risk is unresolved and CET1 will be pressured further by the RAC Insurance WA acquisition; NZI is in structural decline; investment income on technical reserves remains rate-sensitive; and A$400m of ongoing technology spend (AI + modernisation) in FY27 may not yield near-term returns — leaving the stock exposed to any perils or macro shock with minimal capital cushion.
bottom_line.what_changes_mind: Bull case confirmed by: (1) RACQI delivering a full-year underlying margin above 13% in FY27; (2) NZI GWP stabilising with margin recovery above 15%; (3) operating cashflow conversion above 90% of underlying insurance profit disclosed in the annual report; and (4) RAC Insurance WA regulatory approval and integration costs tracking to plan. Bear case confirmed by: a major perils event exhausting the A$1bn volatility cover, reserve strengthening in IIA long-tail lines, or CET1 falling below 0.95x requiring an equity raise.

executive_summary: EBITS collapsed 36.1% to $492.3m (F25: $770.3m) as all three divisions deteriorated sharply — Treasury Americas EBITS fell 61.4% to $90.2m, Treasury Collective fell 47.8% to $68.0m, and even the crown-jewel Penfolds fell 15.2% to $404.3m — driven by deliberate shipment restrictions, distributor transition disruption, and softer category trends

The one thing investors must focus on: TWE recognised $1,308.7m in post-tax material items (impairment of US assets $866.3m + Ascent restructuring $478.9m including $458.6m for the decision to reduce US vintage makes), destroying book value by $1.45bn and producing a statutory NPAT loss of $1,078.7m — this is not a one-off in the classic sense; it reflects structural destruction of value in the Americas business that was built through acquisitions (DAOU etc.) at premium prices

Red flag: The Penfolds China depletion growth figure of +34.7% is materially inflated — management discloses in the footnotes that approximately half of the growth rate was driven by diverting parallel imports into authorised channels, meaning genuine underlying consumer demand growth was closer to ~17%; simultaneously, China customer inventory rebalancing is only half complete (0.2m of 0.4m cases), creating a continued shipment headwind into F27

key_numbers.revenue: NSR $2,561.0m vs F25 $2,938.1m, down 12.8% reported / 11.2% constant currency; volume down 9.9% to 19.2m cases
key_numbers.ebitda_margin: EBITDAS $657.5m (F25: $936.8m), implied EBITDAS margin ~25.7% vs ~31.9% pcp; EBITS margin 19.2% vs 26.2% pcp, down 7.0ppts
key_numbers.npat_statutory: Loss of $1,078.7m vs profit of $436.8m in F25 — swing of $1,515.5m
key_numbers.npat_underlying: NPAT before material items and SGARA $275.3m vs $470.6m, down 41.5%; difference to statutory ($1,354.0m) driven by $1,308.7m post-tax material items (US asset impairments $866.3m + Ascent restructuring $478.9m net of RNDC settlement $19.6m gain) and $60.4m SGARA loss; material items are disclosed but the pre-tax gross charge of ~$1,712.2m is striking
key_numbers.eps: Underlying EPS (pre material items/SGARA) 34.1 cents vs 58.0 cents, down 41.3%; Statutory EPS (133.4) cents vs +53.8 cents pcp
key_numbers.operating_cashflow: Net operating cash flows before financing costs, tax and material items $535.3m vs $819.2m pcp, down 34.7%; cash conversion 81.4% vs 87.4% pcp — declining but still reasonable
key_numbers.free_cashflow: Cash flows after net capex but before financing/tax/material items $436.9m vs $655.5m pcp; cash flows before dividends and material items $194.5m vs $390.9m pcp; no explicit FCF after all items disclosed but total cash flows from activities before debt were negative $(54.8)m vs positive $43.1m pcp
key_numbers.net_debt_cash: Net debt (including lease liabilities) $1,782.4m vs $1,778.9m at June 2025 — essentially flat despite large impairments; interest-bearing debt alone $1,531.1m vs $1,682.8m; cash fell sharply to $221.8m from $427.7m; leverage 2.8x EBITDAS (management states this is the peak)

analysis.quality_of_earnings: Cash conversion of 81.4% (vs 87.4% pcp) is acceptable at face value but masks significant working capital drag ($106.1m outflow) and the RNDC inventory repurchase — TWE bought back California inventory at original sale value and resold ~40% in 2H26 at nil gross margin, artificially inflating COGS per case by 12.2% in Treasury Americas and depressing margins; this nil-margin resale revenue (~$50-60m estimated) is included in NSR, flattering revenue but not earnings. Non-current inventory rose $7.1m to $1,502.4m despite massive write-downs, suggesting further inventory risk. The $1,712.2m pre-tax material items charge (partially non-cash impairments of PP&E, goodwill and inventory) reflects genuine economic destruction, not timing; ROCE fell to 7.9% (vs 11.9%) even after management helpfully excludes US impairments from the capital employed denominator — on a true IFRS capital base, ROCE would be materially lower.
analysis.management_framing: Promotional/Mixed — the release leads with 'business momentum improving' and headlines Penfolds depletion growth of +34.7% in China without immediately disclosing that ~half is parallel import channel diversion, a significant qualification buried in footnote 1. Management frames all volume/revenue declines as 'deliberate' or 'strategic' (brand health, channel health) rather than acknowledging structural demand headwinds and distribution missteps. The dividend cancellation (down 100% to nil vs 40 cents pcp) receives no dedicated headline — a $162.3m dividend was paid in F26 from prior year but no F26 final dividend is declared, a major cash preservation move that is downplayed. The F27 EBITS guidance of 'at least equivalent to F26' sounds constructive but relies heavily on $40m Ascent savings and is heavily second-half weighted (~55%), with Americas EBITS guided to ~$50m (vs $109.4m in F26 under new regional reporting) — implying further Americas deterioration that is not prominently highlighted.
positives: Penfolds remains the genuine earnings engine with a 40.5% EBITS margin ($404.3m), and Greater China EBITS grew sequentially — 1H26 $106.2m vs 2H26 $158.6m (full year $264.8m) — demonstrating real underlying demand recovery momentum as inventory rebalancing progresses; China market share gains are independently measured (Nielsen/Smartpath: online +2.4ppts to 15.7%, offline +1.9ppts to 8.1%)

Balance sheet liquidity is adequate with $1.3bn total liquidity (cash + undrawn facilities) and leverage of 2.8x guided as peak; capex is being cut sharply to ~$75m in F27 from $113.4m in F26, and debt maturities average 3.2 years, providing runway for the deleveraging plan without near-term refinancing pressure
negatives: The Americas business has been structurally impaired — Treasury Americas EBITS margin collapsed from 32.0% to 15.7%, the division generated only $90.2m EBITS on $575m NSR, and F27 Americas EBITS is guided at ~$50m (under new regional model equivalent $109.4m in F26), meaning further halving; $1.3bn+ in US asset write-downs across two tranches plus the decision to reduce vintage makes from 2026 signals the DAOU/luxury US strategy has materially underperformed; the strategic review (with advisors appointed) implies potential distressed asset sales

The nil-dividend in F26, combined with a $30.5m on-market buyback conducted during the period (poor capital allocation given leverage of 2.8x and a statutory loss of $1.08bn), rising working capital drag, and the need to sell through ~60% of remaining RNDC repurchased inventory at nil margin in 1H27 means earnings will be front-loaded with losses — 1H27 EBITS is guided to be only ~45% of the full year (~$221m), implying a very weak first half; the $125m NSR inventory reduction still needed ex-California (0.3m cases) will suppress Americas revenue through 1H28

bottom_line.bull: If Penfolds China depletions normalise into genuine shipment recovery in F27 (China EBITS guided $280-310m, up ~6-17% on F26's $264.8m), Ascent delivers its $40m cost save, and the Americas strategic review crystallises value through asset sales that accelerate deleveraging, TWE could exit F28 with leverage below 2.0x, resumed dividends, and a cleaner, higher-margin portfolio trading on Penfolds' luxury brand premium — a re-rating catalyst.
bottom_line.bear: The Americas impairments may not be the last — the strategic review could reveal further write-downs, the 25% depletion growth in China embeds a channel-shift component that fades, parallel import risk re-emerges, the US wine category continues to structurally decline (19 Crimes depletions -9.1% in the US), and TWE is forced to sell Americas brands at distressed valuations to deleverage, permanently reducing the earnings base; leverage stays elevated beyond F28 if free cash flow disappoints, putting refinancing risk back on the table.
bottom_line.what_changes_mind: Evidence that Penfolds China shipments (not just depletions) are recovering in 1H27 without reliance on parallel-import channel diversion; a credible Americas strategic review outcome (trade sale of brand portfolio or winery assets at reasonable multiples) that materially reduces net debt toward 2.0x ahead of F28; and Treasury Collective Premium portfolio depletions stabilising — the current -9.1% in the US and -11.9% in the UK signal broader brand erosion beyond manageable.
